lit.\u0027¿Qué efecto tiene una insaturación: "What effect does a cis unsaturation in the tail of a phospholipid have?"
lit.\u0027\u003cp class=\"small\"\u003e¿Cómo:
"

How does it cross the bilayer? "
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl \u003cb\u003ecoles:
"

Cholesterol inserts between the phospholipids: its rigid ring orders the tails in the fluid state (less permeability) and prevents crystallization in the gel. At ≈ 30 % it forms a liquid-ordered phase.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa \u003cb\u003eNa⁺/K:
"

The Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase removes 3 Na⁺ and brings in 2 K⁺ for each ATP hydrolyzed, maintaining the cell's gradients. In the simulation the gradient dissipated by the channels is restored.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003ePequeñas moléculas ap:
"

Small nonpolar molecules (O₂, CO₂) cross by simple diffusion. Ions (K⁺) need a selective channel and glucose a facilitated transporter (GLUT); both go down the gradient, without ATP expenditure.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003ePor debajo de la \u00:
"

Below the transition temperature Tm the tails are ordered and extended (gel); above it they move and the bilayer is fluid (lateral diffusion ≈ 1 µm²/s). Tm rises with tail length and falls with unsaturations.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003ePor el \u003cb\u003ee:
"

Because of the hydrophobic effect the tails avoid water. Single-tail amphiphiles (cone) form micelles; two-tailed phospholipids (cylinder) form bilayers, which close into liposomes so as not to expose edges to water.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eUn \u003cb\u003eglice:
"

A glycerophospholipid (here phosphatidylcholine) has a polar head (choline–phosphate–glycerol) and two hydrocarbon tails bound by ester bonds. It is amphipathic. A cis unsaturation (double bond) produces a kink in the tail that prevents compact packing.

"
lit.\u0027A favor del gradiente: difusión si: "Down the gradient: simple diffusion, channels and transporters"
lit.\u0027Agrega colesterol y repite: el cam: 'Add cholesterol and repeat: the change in fluidity is more gradual.'
lit.\u0027Amortigua la fluidez: ordena lo fl: "Buffers fluidity: orders the fluid and disorders the gel"
lit.\u0027cabeza hidrofílica, cola hidrofóbi: 'hydrophilic head, hydrophobic tail, water, cholesterol, cis-unsaturation kink and transport proteins.'
lit.\u0027Cabeza polar hidrofílica y dos col: "Hydrophilic polar head and two nonpolar tails"
lit.\u0027Cambia de escena en «Lab»: lípido,: "Change scene in “Lab”: lipid, assembly, bilayer (temperature, cholesterol) and transport (with or without ATP)."
lit.\u0027Colas más largas → Tm mayor; cada: "Longer tails → higher Tm; each cis double bond → much lower Tm."
lit.\u0027Desafío: ¿cómo cruza la membrana?\: "Challenge: how does it cross the membrane?"
lit.\u0027Difusión simple: gases y moléculas: "Simple diffusion: gases and nonpolar molecules; channels and GLUT: down the gradient."
lit.\u0027El codo impide el empaquetamiento: "The kink prevents compact packing of the tails."
lit.\u0027elimina la carga de la cabeza\u002: "it removes the charge of the head"
lit.\u0027En «Transporte» quita el ATP: la b: 'In transport remove the ATP: the Na⁺/K⁺ pump stops, but O₂ and glucose still move down their gradient.'
lit.\u0027En agua, las colas se esconden: mi: "In water, the tails hide: micelle, bilayer or liposome"
lit.\u0027En contra del gradiente, con ATP:: "Against the gradient, with ATP: Na⁺/K⁺ pump"
lit.\u0027En la bicapa baja la temperatura b: 'In the bilayer lower the temperature below Tm: the tails become ordered (gel); raise it and they disorder (fluid).'
lit.\u0027Es electrogénica: saca una carga p: "It is electrogenic: it removes one net positive charge per cycle."
lit.\u0027Es pequeño y apolar: se disuelve e: "It is small and nonpolar: it dissolves in the hydrophobic interior."
lit.\u0027Es polar y grande: necesita una pr: "It is polar and large: it needs a protein, but not energy."
lit.\u0027Escala logarítmica (µm²/s): la tra: "Logarithmic scale (µm²/s): the gel → fluid transition raises D by ≈ 2–3 orders of magnitude."
lit.\u0027introduce un codo, baja la Tm y au: "it introduces a kink, lowers the Tm and increases fluidity"
lit.\u0027La bomba Na⁺/K⁺ usa ATP para ir \u: "The Na⁺/K⁺ pump uses ATP to go against the gradient (3 Na⁺ out, 2 K⁺ in)."
lit.\u0027La glucosa entra a favor de su gra: "Glucose enters a cell down its gradient through…"
lit.\u0027Las \u003cb\u003einsaturaciones ci: "Cis unsaturations and short tails lower the Tm (more fluidity)."
lit.\u0027Las colas extendidas y empaquetada: "Extended and packed tails reduce lateral diffusion."
lit.\u0027Los fosfolípidos tienen cabeza pol: "Phospholipids have a polar head and nonpolar tails."
lit.\u0027orden de las colas frente a la tem: 'tail order versus temperature, lateral diffusion, transition temperature (Tm) and relative permeability of the bilayer.'
lit.\u0027ordena o desordena las colas según: "orders or disorders the tails according to Tm."
lit.\u0027partículas O₂, glucosa, Na⁺ y K⁺ c: "O₂, glucose, Na⁺ and K⁺ particles with membrane proteins."
lit.\u0027Permeabilidad relativa de la bicap: "Relative permeability of the bilayer (orders of magnitude)"
lit.\u0027Por debajo de su Tm, una bicapa li: "Below its Tm, a lipid bilayer is in the state…"
lit.\u0027S_CD (parámetro de orden): alto =: "S_CD (order parameter): high = gel, low = fluid. Dotted line: Tm. With cholesterol the transition broadens."
lit.\u0027Su anillo rígido restringe el movi: "Its rigid ring restricts the movement of neighboring tails."
lit.\u0027Su forma cilíndrica favorece lámin: "Their cylindrical shape favors sheets; they close into vesicles to hide the edges."
lit.\u0027tiene una parte hidrofílica y otra: "has a hydrophilic part and a hydrophobic part"
lit.\u0027Valores ilustrativos de log₁₀ P (c: "Illustrative values of log₁₀ P (cm/s): gases and nonpolar molecules cross easily; ions hardly at all without proteins."
